pr.title: Spend the verification time on logons to unknown accounts (Argon2id review)
pr.body:
## Summary

This is the Phase 1 **Argon2id password hashing review**. The hashing itself holds up; the review found one issue, **user enumeration by timing**, which this PR fixes.

## Review

| Area | Finding |
|---|---|
| **Algorithm and cost** | Argon2id by default with 19 MiB of memory, 2 iterations and 1 lane, OWASP's recommended minimum. PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations when selected. Both through OpenSSL. ✅ |
| **Salt and hash** | A random 16-byte salt per hash, a 32-byte hash, stored in PHC string format. ✅ |
| **Comparison** | `CRYPTO_memcmp`, constant time. ✅ |
| **Parsing limits** | Stored costs are bounded (memory 4 MiB–1 GiB, iterations 1–20, PBKDF2 10,000–10,000,000), and hash lengths the code can't produce are rejected. ✅ |
| **Upgrade path** | Hashes with another algorithm or cost, and legacy MD5, SHA-256, Blowfish or plain values, are replaced at the next successful logon when auto-upgrade is on (the default for new installations). ✅ Accounts that never log on keep their legacy hash. |
| **Memory under load** | Each Argon2id verification allocates about 19 MiB, but logons run on the fixed pool of TCP/IP threads (15 by default), so the total stays bounded at about 285 MiB. ✅ No change. |
| **Timing** | ❌ A logon to an account that doesn't exist, or is inactive, or whose domain is missing or inactive, was refused **before any password was verified**. A wrong password for a real account costs a full Argon2id verification (tens of milliseconds), so how long a failed logon took revealed which accounts exist. **Fixed here.** |

## Fix

- **`PasswordHasher::SpendVerificationTime`** verifies the password against a dummy hash that belongs to no account, and ignores the result. The dummy is made with the configured algorithm and cost, and made again whenever the administrator changes them, so it always costs the same as a real account's verification. The check runs outside the lock, so parallel logons don't queue behind each other.
- **`PasswordValidator`** calls it on each of the four early refusals: no account, account inactive, no domain, domain inactive.

## Test

`Security.LogonTiming.TestUnknownAccountFailsAsSlowlyAsWrongPassword` switches the server to Argon2id at the default cost and times five failed POP3 logons of each kind. The fastest logon to an unknown account must take at least half as long as the fastest with a wrong password; taking the fastest filters out connection noise. On the old code the unknown account takes a small fraction of the time.

commit.message:
Spend the verification time on logons to unknown accounts

Reviewing the Argon2id password hashing found one issue: a logon to an
account that does not exist, is not active, or is in a domain that does not
exist or is not active was refused before any password was verified, while one
with a wrong password costs an Argon2id verification - tens of milliseconds at
the default cost. The time a failed logon took told which accounts exist.

PasswordHasher::SpendVerificationTime verifies the password against a hash of
no account, made with the configured algorithm and cost - again whenever they
change - and PasswordValidator calls it on each of those refusals, so every
failed logon takes as long.

Security.LogonTiming checks it with the default Argon2id cost: the fastest of
five failed logons to an unknown account takes at least half as long as the
fastest of five with a wrong password. Before, it took a small fraction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
